title: InferQ: A Database-Oriented Benchmark for Quantum Circuits Simulation
authors: Andrei Ilinescu, Aadi Patwardhan, Rihan Hai
abstract: Recent work suggests that relational database management systems (RDBMSs) can execute quantum circuit simulation by compiling the simulation into SQL workloads (primarily join-and-aggregate tensor contractions). While early results are promising, they largely focus on a narrow set of highly structured circuits and offer limited support for systematic database research, such as query optimization, physical design, and engine-level evaluation across a broad range of circuits. We present InferQ, a database-oriented benchmark for quantum circuit simulation. InferQ generates general, compositional circuits by assembling subcircuits from a set of circuit templates, emits each simulation task as an RDBMS-ready SQL workload, and extracts circuit and query features (static, graph, SQL, and dynamic) for workload characterization. InferQ also releases a large dataset of 202,975 circuits online, with a web-based viewer to support searching, filtering, and downloading circuits and feature records. In experiments across RDBMS engines (PostgreSQL, SQLite, DuckDB, and Umbra) and the widely used Qiskit Aer simulator, we find that RDBMSs achieve better peak memory usage than Qiskit Aer on more than 50% of the circuits generated by InferQ. Moreover, using InferQ features, lightweight machine learning models (linear and tree-based models) can accurately predict when SQL execution is preferable (with accuracy up to 95.3% for runtime and 97.4% for memory), enabling data-centric simulator selection and opening the door to principled optimization of SQL-based quantum circuit simulation.
summary: This paper introduces InferQ, a comprehensive benchmark designed to test quantum circuit simulation by translating computations into SQL workloads executable on RDBMSs. It systematically generates diverse circuits and extracts rich features, demonstrating that database engines can offer competitive performance metrics like memory usage compared to standard simulators. This work opens the door for data-centric optimization of quantum algorithms by predicting the best execution backend.
main_problem: The authors developed a systematic benchmark, InferQ, to evaluate quantum circuit simulation performance when executed using Relational Database Management Systems (RDBMSs) compared to standard simulators.
main_result: InferQ demonstrated that RDBMSs can achieve better peak memory usage than Qiskit Aer on over 50% of tested circuits, and machine learning models trained on its features can accurately predict the optimal simulation engine.
method: The method involves generating general, compositional quantum circuits, translating each simulation task into an RDBMS-ready SQL workload (tensor contractions), and extracting comprehensive static, graph, and SQL features for analysis.
model_or_system: The system under study is the quantum circuit model, where states are represented by complex vectors. The computation is simulated either via standard quantum simulators or by compiling the operations into join-and-aggregate tensor contractions executed within an RDBMS.
key_observables: Peak memory usage, execution runtime, classification accuracy (for predicting optimal backend), and various circuit/SQL features (e.g., graph diameter, number of JOINs).
important_parameters: The benchmark covers a large dataset of 202,975 circuits generated by composing subcircuits from templates.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that quantum circuit simulation can be systematically mapped onto SQL workloads suitable for database analysis. The ML predictions rely on the completeness and diversity of the extracted features.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate feature distributions (static, graph, SQL), performance comparisons between RDBMSs and Qiskit Aer, and machine learning model performance metrics showing high prediction accuracy.
paper_structure: The paper introduces InferQ to address the lack of systematic benchmarks. It details circuit generation via template composition, workload extraction into SQL, feature engineering (static/graph/SQL), comparative experiments across multiple RDBMSs vs. Qiskit Aer, and finally, using ML models to predict optimal execution backends.
why_interesting: While focused on database performance, the systematic benchmarking of quantum circuits provides a novel computational resource analysis framework that could inform hardware-aware algorithm design or compiler optimization for future quantum computing architectures.

Figure 4 illustrates one end-to-end circuit instance generated by InferQ. The workflow is intentionally analogous to a database benchmark that (i) samples a scale/configuration, (ii) instantiates a small sequence of templates with parameters, and (iii) materializes both an artifact and its metadata.
